handwriting-to-font-converter.formula:
Each glyph is stored as a list of pen strokes.
Each stroke is a list of points (x, y), normalised to 0..1 across the drawing pad.

Preview rendering for a typed character C at font size F:
  for each stroke S of C:
    draw polyline through points (originX + x*F, originY + y*F)
  advance originX by F * 0.72

Undrawn characters fall back to a grey system letter.
SVG export writes each stroke as a <polyline> in a labelled grid.
howTo: Pick a letter in the character grid - start with capitals A to Z.
Draw the letter on the pad with your mouse, touch, or stylus. Each drag is one stroke.
Use Undo or Clear letter if a stroke goes wrong; the preview updates live.
Type any text in the preview box to see it rendered in your handwriting.
Export the preview as a PNG image or your whole alphabet as an SVG sheet.
keyFacts: You draw each character once on a guided pad; the tool stores your pen strokes.
Every stroke is saved as a list of points, so letters redraw crisply at any size.
The preview typesets your text by replaying the stored strokes for each character.
Characters you have not drawn yet appear as grey system letters.
69 characters are supported: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and . , ! ? ' -.
PNG export captures the preview; SVG export captures your whole drawn alphabet as vectors.

handwriting-to-font-converter.workedExample:
Drawing the letter 'A':
1. Select 'A' in the character grid.
2. Drag once for the left diagonal: points (0.3, 0.8) -> (0.5, 0.2).
3. Drag again for the right diagonal: points (0.7, 0.8) -> (0.5, 0.2).
4. Drag a third time for the crossbar: points (0.38, 0.55) -> (0.62, 0.55).

Stored: 3 strokes, each a list of normalised (x, y) points.

Previewing 'A' at size 56:
  Each stroke is replayed as a polyline scaled by 56 px.
  Stroke 1 renders from (16.8, 44.8) to (28, 11.2).
  Undrawn letters (say 'B') appear as grey system letters until you draw them.

Export: the PNG captures this preview; the SVG writes all 3 strokes as <polyline> elements.
